mechanism_narrative: Sustained low federal funds rates (FEDFUNDS ≤ 0.07%) compress equity discount rates, generating positive S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days as future cash flows are valued more heavily.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in > 40% of instances where FEDFUNDS ≤ 0.07% (t-test p > 0.05 for mean return > 0).

mechanism_narrative: Unemployment rates exceeding 8.0% signal labor market weakness, reducing consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, driving negative S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in > 60% of instances where UNRATE > 8.0 (t-test p > 0.05 for mean return < 0).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous housing starts below 680 (HOUST < 680) and GDP growth contraction (GDPC1 < 13000) indicate weakening consumer demand, triggering negative S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in > 50% of instances where HOUST < 680 and GDPC1 < 13000 (t-test p > 0.05 for mean return < 0).

mechanism_narrative: Monetary tightening cycles (FEDFUNDS > 0.05%) increase equity discount rates, reducing present value of future earnings and producing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in > 55% of instances where FEDFUNDS > 0.05 (t-test p > 0.05 for mean return < 0).

mechanism_narrative: Payroll employment growth (PAYEMS rising) indicates robust labor market conditions, increasing consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 returns over 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in > 45% of instances where PAYEMS is rising (t-test p > 0.05 for mean return > 0).

mechanism_narrative: Industrial production below 90 (INDPRO < 90) reflects manufacturing contraction, reducing corporate output and earnings growth, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in > 50% of instances where INDPRO < 90 (t-test p > 0.05 for mean return < 0).

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent inflation above 2.5% (CPIAUCSL > 2.5) and housing starts decline (HOUST < 680) indicate inflationary demand pressure with weakening consumer activity, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in > 55% of instances where CPIAUCSL > 2.5 and HOUST < 680 (t-test p > 0.05 for mean return < 0).

mechanism_narrative: Late-cycle expansion (UNRATE < 5.0 and HOUST > 700) indicates overvalued economy with high interest rates, triggering negative S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days as market corrects.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in > 50% of instances where UNRATE < 5.0 and HOUST > 700 (t-test p > 0.05 for mean return < 0).
